subject: Jurisdictional-hold and 'tombstone' deletion process — DPA redlines
messages:
From: Heather Lane <heather.lane@acme-media.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@acme-media.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:11:00 -0800
Subject: DPA redlines: jurisdictional hold, deletion windows, and 'tombstone' wording

Sergio —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the DPA. Our legal team reviewed and flagged three sticking points we need clearer language on before we can proceed:

1) Jurisdictional hold: we need a concrete mechanism to preserve EU customer data when a legal/ regulatory hold is issued (e.g., preservation for e-discovery). Please confirm you can:
   - Place a hold that prevents deletion from primary and backup copies for the duration of the hold;
   - Surface audible audit logs showing hold start/stop and the scope.

2) Deletion windows: your current redline language refers to a 30-day "reasonable time" to delete backups. We are asking for: 30 days for live production data and a maximum of 90 days for backups unless a legal hold applies.

3) 'Tombstone' definition and certification: the DPA uses the term tombstone but doesn't define it. We need confirmation whether tombstoning is reversible (soft delete) or irreversible (cryptographic erasure). We also want a deletion certificate (signed) containing a fingerprint or audit reference for each erasure.

I've attached ACME_DPA_Redline_v3.docx with inline comments and a proposed clause on deletion certification.

A couple of questions to help us align:
- Does your backup policy differentiate by geography (e.g., EU backups kept onshore)?
- Do you offer an expedited export for data subject requests or legal holds, and what's the SLT for exports?

Can we set a short conference with your security team tomorrow?

—Heather
Heather Lane
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Acme Media

Heather —

Thanks for the detailed notes and the redline doc — appreciate the clarity. High-level responses below and then a proposal for compromise language. Karthik (Security & Compliance) and Marissa (AE) are looped in.

1) Jurisdictional hold: yes, we support legal holds. Practically we implement a scoped hold that:
   - prevents normal retention-driven deletions on primary stores;
   - flags associated backups so that they are excluded from the expiration job; and
   - records an immutable audit event (hold id, start time, scope, requestor) visible in the Console's audit trail.

2) Deletion windows: our standard is 30 days for primary/active data and 60 days for backups (disaster recovery cadence). We're open to 60 days for backups for customers that need it, and to commit to providing a deletion certification after the final wipe. We cannot commit to 90-day backups by default without pricing/operational adjustments, but we can offer that as an option for EU customers (Dedicated or Private) or via a contractual exception at the enterprise tier.

3) Tombstone: in Redwood's terminology our "tombstone" is initially a logical delete marker (soft delete) followed by a scheduled irreversible step we call "cryptographic tombstone" — the latter consists of key-schedule rotation and key-eviction that renders ciphertext unrecoverable. We also perform metadata purge workflows (index removal, KV cache purge). We will produce a deletion certificate that references the job id, timestamp, and audit log link.

Attached is a short tech note with the process (redwood-tombstone-process.pdf).

Proposal for compromise language (suggested DPA snippet):
"For data located in the EU, Redwood will retain primary customer data for a maximum of 30 days from deletion request and retain backups for no more than 60 days, unless a documented legal hold is in effect. For customers requiring a 90-day backup window, Redwood will offer this as a configured option subject to commercial terms. Upon customer request, Redwood will execute the irreversible cryptographic-tombstone process and will provide a deletion certificate containing an audit reference and checksum within 10 business days of completion."

If that looks workable we can:
- Produce a tracked-redline of the DPA with the above snippet;
- Book a 30-min call with Karthik to walk through the delete/cert process and the Console audit outputs.

When would Heather/your legal be available tomorrow (Wed) 8–12 PT?

Thanks — Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: DPA redlines: jurisdictional hold, deletion windows, and 'tombstone' wording

Sergio —

Thanks for the quick reply and the process note — that helps. A few follow-ups after an internal sync:

- Backup window: Acme's position is we need the option to set a 90-day backup retention for EU production data at no additional cost as a baseline for our category of regulated customers. If you can't make it baseline, we need clear pricing and the SLA to ensure it's always available.

- Immutability and audit: the backups retained under a legal hold must be immutable (WORM-like) while the hold is active. Additionally, the deletion certificate must contain a SHA256 fingerprint (or similar) of the item(s) and a signed statement from Redwood that identifies the job id and the storage locations purged.

- Tombstone semantics: we need the DPA to define two terms: "soft tombstone" (reversible, 30-day window) and "cryptographic tombstone" (irreversible, key-eviction based) and to require that the cryptographic tombstone be used for EU customer-data erasure unless a legal hold prevents it.

- Environments: confirm that staging/test environments do not inherit production retention exceptions unless explicitly requested.

We'll attach our annotated version to ACME_DPA_Redline_v3.docx. If you can produce a tracked change that incorporates the definitions above and the certificate format we can get an internal sign-off faster.

Would Karthik be able to provide the cert template and the exact Console audit key names so our ops team can validate against them?

—Heather

Heather —

Appreciate the thoughtful asks. Below are concrete technical commitments and a proposed certificate template you can paste into the DPA. Happy to jump on a call to walk through any item.

Technical commitments and clarifications:
1) Hold implementation:
   - When a hold is created we set a "hold" flag across services (primary index, backups, and object-store metadata). Expiration jobs explicitly skip objects with an active hold flag.
   - The hold is recorded as an immutable audit event (hold_id, requestor, start_ts, scope list, reason). Audit events are exportable via Console and via API.

2) Backup immutability:
   - Backups under a legal hold are retained in write-once mode: the backup manifest is marked immutable and retention is enforced by the storage layer.

3) Tombstone / cryptographic erase flow (sequence):
   - Step A: logical delete / soft tombstone (metadata flag, 30-day reversible window by default).
   - Step B: KV-cache purge and index removal (immediate).
   - Step C: cryptographic tombstone (key-eviction & re-wrap): keys protecting the object are scheduled for rotation and removal; once keys are evicted the object ciphertext is unrecoverable.
   - Step D: final metadata purge / manifest removal and job recording.

4) Deletion certificate (proposed minimal schema — you can paste into contract):
   - Certificate ID: <cert-id>
   - Customer: Acme Media
   - Subject(s) erased: list of object ids / logical ids
   - Job ID: <job-id>
   - Timestamp (UTC): <iso-ts>
   - Method: cryptographic-tombstone (key-eviction)
   - Fingerprint: SHA256 <hex> (where applicable)
   - Audit log ref: https://redwood.app/audit/<audit-id>
   - Signed-by: Redwood Inference (security ops)

5) Onshore processing and exports:
   - For EU data we can guarantee onshore processing (EU-only storage) in the Dedicated/Private deployments. For Hosted accounts, we can commit to regionally-segregated storage in the EU region and will provide exports within 5 business days unless a legal hold blocks export.

6) Staging/test environments:
   - Staging and test do not inherit production retention exceptions by default; they are separate projects. If Acme requests parity we will add explicit configuration and note it in the DPA annex.

Next steps: I'll prepare a tracked-change DPA snippet that includes the soft/cryptographic tombstone definitions plus the certificate template and the 60 vs 90-day options as toggles. Sergio/Marissa — I'll ping you with a draft this evening and propose a 30-min call Fri 9–11 PT.

Thanks — Karthik
